slides.notes: Aqion Relay helps a non-perishable goods distributor compare recovery purchases against an owner-defined cash floor. The public MVP uses fictional SME and supplier data. It trains a numerical forecast, evaluates feasible alternatives and saves an unsent draft only after owner confirmation. No order is sent and no funds move. The two cover links take judges directly to the public source and the verified live demonstration.

slides.title: A recovery choice you can inspect.
slides.notes: Reference fixture: packaging SME; shipment delay 7 days; demand increase 20%; freight increase 25%; cash floor AED 24,000. The model evaluates 130 combinations including baseline. Baseline fulfilment is 990 of 1,362 projected units with 9 stockout days. The recommended evaluated order is 400 units from fictional Oasis, arriving on day 4. It costs AED 7,887.50 including fictional VAT-inclusive item price and adjusted freight. It fulfils 1,362 projected units with zero stockout days and minimum projected cash AED 28,112.50. These are model outputs on fiction, not measured customer gains. Model assumptions include prepaid original inbound stock, recovery paid on day 1, scheduled receipts only and obligations before same-day receipts.

slides.title:
Forecast numerically.
Decide within hard constraints.
slides.notes: The forecast fits weekday and trend ridge regression to fictional fulfilled-sales history, comparing the last 14 days against a seasonal-naive baseline; it chooses the lower synthetic holdout-error method and refits as applicable. Short or constant histories use a labelled trailing-average fallback. The same holdout is used for model selection, so it is not an independent final quality test. Fulfilled sales may censor true demand. Candidate quantities obey approved-supplier status, quote expiry, MOQ, pack size, cap and lead time. Enumeration is bounded, at most 8,000 combinations in the current three-supplier slice, not a proof of a global optimum. Deterministic templates explain the calculation; no live generative model decides purchases.

slides.title:
One deployment.
Persistent, isolated demo workspaces.
slides.notes: The production deployment uses a static-export Next.js/React frontend served as Cloudflare Worker assets. The API, numerical engine and domain services run inside a native SQLite-backed Durable Object, using transactionSync for atomic draft, audit and version checks. Signed anonymous sessions, same-origin/CSRF controls and bounded inputs guard the public synthetic workflow. A workspace transaction preserves approval and audit integrity. This is not enterprise tenant IAM; the production-pilot roadmap adds authenticated roles, approved processing/data location, connector credentials and operational restore acceptance. No local filesystem database or Hostinger/MySQL service is required for the Cloudflare release.

slides.title:
Read first. Reconcile every write.
Then expand through du.
slides.notes: Proposed eight-week integration preparation, with responsibilities and acceptance gates. Weeks 1–2: AqionLabs maps consented snapshots, SME owners verify terms and the du sponsor approves scope; gate is required-field coverage and approved processing/security design. Weeks 3–4: AqionLabs builds a scoped read-only Zoho adapter using organization and region context; reconcile normalized snapshot against source totals and handle event IDs/revisions. Weeks 5–6: add owner-authorized ERP drafts with idempotency/outbox and reconciliation, sandbox-tested; ambiguous writes remain pending reconciliation. Weeks 7–8: configure sponsor-agreed du identity/billing/distribution interfaces and operational monitoring; no du interface is claimed connected. Each period starts when its dependencies are approved. Pilot comparison begins only after acceptance. Odoo is a subsequent adapter subject to exact version/plan, not a prerequisite for the first pilot.

slides.title:
160 SMEs. Four waves.
A credible comparison.
slides.notes: Proposed enrollment: 160 consenting non-perishable-goods distributors; at least 150 enrolled before intervention. du sponsors recruitment; AqionLabs operates onboarding, support and analysis; an evaluation lead preregisters outcomes and completes power/MDE analysis before intervention. Four waves of 40 start in pilot weeks 1,2,3,4. Each receives two common baseline weeks then six comparison weeks; within each wave and sector/size/ERP strata, randomize 20 immediate and 20 delayed-access SMEs. The last comparison ends in week 11, analysis occurs in week 12. Delayed access follows its comparison window. Enrollment begins after the integration and operational acceptance gates, not during an unsafe live-write trial. Record screened, enrolled, randomized, activated, completed, withdrawn and missing-data counts; do not replace dropouts after randomization. A 160-SME feasibility cohort alone does not establish statistical power.

slides.title:
Measure better decisions.
Keep operational guardrails absolute.
slides.notes: All percentages on this slide are prospective pilot targets, not achieved customer outcomes. Primary outcome: time from equivalent disruption brief to owner-approved plan that passes a predetermined blinded feasibility rubric. Use baseline-adjusted log-time comparison with SME assignment, wave/calendar and strata; report effect and 95% interval plus raw medians. Include non-completion under a preregistered capped-time rule with sensitivity analysis. Target 40% shorter time. Secondary feasibility target: at least 90% rubric-passing approved plans, all assigned drills in denominator. Adoption target: 70% of SMEs with access review at least one scenario per week, reporting opportunity and reasons for non-use. Exploratory stockout target is 15% reduction, reported separately with uncertainty and no causal before/after shortcut. Zero projected floor breaches, unauthorized external writes and duplicate external effects are stop rules for the later live pilot, not claims that predicted cash guarantees actual cash. Monitor source completeness and reconciliation latency. Independent baseline variance/power analysis determines whether efficacy or feasibility interpretation is justified.

slides.title:
A narrow wedge.
A repeatable route through du.
slides.notes: Commercial proposal: a per-SME subscription distributed through du, with connector onboarding and service scope agreed before offer. No price, revenue, customer count or commercial commitment is claimed. Measure onboarding time, weekly use, support minutes and total cost per active SME in the pilot; scale only within a sponsor-approved unit-cost ceiling. Engineering scale path: 160-SME pilot, a 1,000-SME controlled rollout, then load/isolation/restore acceptance for the 40,000+ ambition. An illustrative engineering envelope assumes 1,000 normalized events and four scenarios per SME per day: 40m events/day at 40,000 SMEs, 463 average events/s, 4,630/s at ten-times peak, and 160,000 scenarios/day (1.85 average/s). These are arithmetic assumptions, not measured capacity. Proposed service targets such as p95 scenario latency <5s, availability 99.9%, RPO<=15m and RTO<=4h require sponsor agreement and separate acceptance tests; they are not current contractual SLAs.

slides.title:
Make the safe action
the easiest action.
slides.notes: Current synthetic MVP controls include validation, source-age and quote checks, scenario/version binding, signed anonymous sessions, same-origin/CSRF checks, bounded input, persistent draft/audit transactions, human confirmation and duplicate protection. These do not constitute enterprise acceptance. Pilot release gates add tenant IAM/roles, approved processing and data location, scoped connector secrets, encryption and restore testing, ERP outbox/reconciliation and incident ownership. Daily monitoring reviews source lag, invalid fields, rejected approvals, write ambiguity and reconciliation age. A material floor/authorization/duplicate violation pauses writes; the operator investigates and the sponsor approves resumption. Forecast error is monitored against naive baseline, sparse histories fall back visibly. No autonomous buying or funds movement is included.
